clue.text: Prepare in advance, being not a full member

definitions.meaning: to arm beforehand, get ready for trouble before it comes
read as FORE plus ARM: only the front part of the arm, so not the whole limb or member

explanation.surface: Someone gets ready early, though they are only an associate rather than a full member of the club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' in the second definition means a limb, not someone in a club; the part of the arm below the elbow is not the full limb.
explanation.definitionFit: To get armed or braced before a danger arrives is a verb meaning prepare beforehand.

clue.text: Endless commotion upset no-one in coalition

indicators.note: endless removes the final letter of the word for commotion

parts.note: fuss means commotion

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: split as NO plus I, the Roman one

explanation.surface: Commotion without end upsets nobody in the governing alliance.
explanation.definitionFit: A merger or blending of parties is a union or alliance.

clue.text: Language in book hard to follow

indicators.note: to follow puts the hard letter after the book

parts.note: Romans is a book of the New Testament
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A language in some volume is hard to keep up with.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rhaeto-Romance tongue of Switzerland is a national language there.

clue.text: For example, insect non-U fellow found on old seed-case

indicators.note: non-U means without the letter U, playing on non-U meaning not upper-class

parts.note: Arthur is a man's name, so any fellow
a pod is the case holding peas or beans

explanation.surface: An insect, say, and a vulgar chap discovered on an ancient pod.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Non-U' is British slang for not upper-class; here it simply drops the U.
explanation.definitionFit: Insects are one class within the jointed-legged invertebrate phylum.

clue.text: Relative with the offensive weapon taken outside? Say nothing!

parts.note: mum is a mother, a relative

indicators.note: the weapon is taken around the outside of the word the

parts.note: a sword is a weapon for attack

explanation.surface: A relative takes a weapon outside, and someone urges silence.
explanation.definitionFit: A command to keep a secret, stay quiet about it.

clue.text: Quickly grab music on way to city

parts.note: a catch is a round, a short song for several voices sung in turn
going up is travelling to the city, especially to London or a university town

explanation.surface: Someone snatches some music on their journey into town.
explanation.walkthrough: A CATCH is an old kind of round sung by several voices; 'up' is the British convention for travel towards the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: To snatch something up hastily is an old sense of seizing it quickly.

clue.text: Island'S damage limitation?

indicators.note: limitation means the end is cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: damage is informal for cost, as in 'what's the damage?'

explanation.surface: An island makes efforts to limit damage.
explanation.definitionFit: A Greek island in the Dodecanese, also spelt Kos.

clue.text: Story about bishop's fellow-diners

indicators.note: about means around, so the story surrounds the bishop

parts.note: a tale is a story
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A tale about a bishop's dinner companions.
explanation.definitionFit: The people seated for a meal together form a company, as in 'the whole board laughed'.

clue.text: Male soldier on campaign given what sounds like foul accommodation

parts.note: he is a male pronoun
NCO is a non-commissioned officer, a soldier
op is short for operation, a military campaign

explanation.surface: A male soldier on campaign gets dreadful quarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foul' is said like 'fowl', so the accommodation is for poultry.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen for hens is housing for poultry, which is fowl.

clue.text: Stimulating people it's less usual to find in pairs

indicators.note: find in places the stranger word inside the abbreviation for pairs

parts.note: PRS is the abbreviation for pairs
odder means stranger, less usual

explanation.surface: It is rarer to find stimulating people in couples.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who poke or goad others into action are rousing people.

clue.text: Thus ran into half-back now and then

parts.note: so means thus, in this way
to run into someone is to meet them

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for half from right to left

parts.note: semi- means half, as in semicircle

explanation.surface: A footballer collided with the half-back every so often.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-back' looks like a football position, but 'half' is SEMI and 'back' turns it into IMES.
explanation.definitionFit: Occasionally, at intervals, is what the phrase means.

clue.text: Game in which sportsman ultimately enters large circle

indicators.note: enters says the final letter goes inside the large circle

parts.note: large means big

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of the word sportsman

parts.note: O is circle-shaped

explanation.surface: In some game, a sportsman finally steps into a big ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A numbers game of calling and marking off cards is a well-known pastime.

clue.text: He has to admit retired engineers

parts.note: to own up is to admit

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British Army's engineering corps

explanation.surface: A man has to confess that the engineers have retired.
explanation.definitionFit: A possessor is someone who has a thing, so 'he has' describes a proprietor.

clue.text: About to cut the pleat in several parts

indicators.note: cut here means the word the is split open by the word for about entering it

parts.note: re means about, concerning
a pleat is a fold in cloth

explanation.surface: Something about to cut a pleat in fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Several' is loose for three, but fair: a threefold division is one into several portions.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripled, made of three portions, is the sense, three being several.

clue.text: Glorious soldiers exhausted containing advance

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are soldiers

indicators.note: containing means the word for exhausted holds the word for advance

parts.note: spent means exhausted
to lend is to advance money

explanation.surface: Proud soldiers worn out after an advance.
explanation.definitionFit: Dazzling and splendid in appearance is magnificent.

clue.text: Insignificant type of thief, one who takes pictures

parts.note: to whip is informal British for to steal, so a whipper is one who steals
a snapper is a photographer, one who takes snaps

explanation.surface: A petty thief turns out to be a photographer.
explanation.definitionFit: An impertinent young nobody is the classic sense of this old word for a presumptuous youngster.

clue.text: Unemotional way to get involved in a call-up

indicators.note: get involved in places the way inside the other letters
up in a down clue means written upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: to cite is to call, summon to court
a path is a way

explanation.surface: An indifferent way to get caught up in military conscription.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing no interest or feeling is listless and indifferent.

clue.text: Exercise quite effectively

parts.note: to exercise a right is to use it
quite means fully, completely

explanation.surface: Working out is quite productive.
explanation.definitionFit: Done to good purpose, practically, is in a helpful way.

clue.text: Officer gives order, and equals put it out

indicators.note: put out means disordered, so the letters before it are thrown into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An officer gives an order, and his equals spoil it.
explanation.definitionFit: An RAF rank between flight lieutenant and wing commander, so an officer.

clue.text: Appropriately treats rotten old sprout?

indicators.note: rotten means decayed, spoiled, so the letters are spoiled into a new order

explanation.surface: A gardener deals properly with a decayed old Brussels sprout.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulling out of the ground by the roots is the fitting treatment for a dead plant.

clue.text: Involve little sibling in climbing tree

indicators.note: in places the sibling inside the reversed tree
climbing in a down clue means rising, so the tree is written upwards

parts.note: a lime is a linden tree
bro is a shortened brother

explanation.surface: A younger brother gets caught up in a tree he is climbing.
explanation.definitionFit: To entangle someone in a dispute is to drag them into it.

clue.text: Accompany and listen carefully

definitions.meaning: to go along with, as a page waits upon a lord
to pay heed, as in '... to what I say'

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: to escort someone, and to give heed.

clue.text: It'S not permitted, oddly, in Bedford

indicators.note: oddly means in a strange way, so the letters are arranged differently

explanation.surface: Something is banned in an odd way in the town of Bedford.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' looks like a pick of odd letters, but here it rearranges IN and BEDFORD together.
explanation.definitionFit: Banned or prohibited things are those not allowed.

clue.text: Part of canal in Troy, as Virgil reported it?

indicators.note: Virgil wrote in Latin, so the name of the city as he would have said it

parts.note: Ilium is the Latin name for Troy

explanation.surface: A section of a waterway in Troy, as told in the Aeneid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canal' suggests a waterway; it is the alimentary canal.
explanation.definitionFit: The final section of the small intestine is part of the gut.

clue.text: Frame of mind at finally leaving natural home

indicators.note: the word at goes away from the end of the longer word

parts.note: a habitat is the natural home of an animal or plant

explanation.surface: A state of mind arrives when an animal at last leaves its native environment.
explanation.definitionFit: A settled disposition or mental make-up is an old sense, as in 'habit of mind'.

clue.text: Approximate points recorded after game

indicators.note: after places the compass points behind the card game

parts.note: loo is an old card game
S and E, south and east, are compass points as written down

explanation.surface: Rough scores are noted down after the match.
explanation.walkthrough: LOO is an old card game; 'loo' is also the British slang for toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose translation is an approximate, not exact, one.

clue.text: Baton initially chosen by English conductor

indicators.note: initially means the word for chosen goes first, before the baton

parts.note: elect means chosen, as in president-elect
a baton is a rod

explanation.surface: An English orchestral conductor picks up a baton he has chosen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conductor' suggests an orchestra; it is an electrical conductor.
explanation.definitionFit: A terminal through which current enters or leaves is an electrical conductor.

clue.text: The Spanish king's deer

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A deer belonging to the Spanish king.
explanation.definitionFit: A large deer, the moose in North America.

clue.text: Use piece of sturdy ash, making cover for clock

indicators.note: a piece of the words sturdy ash making is taken from within them

explanation.surface: Using a chunk of tough ash wood to make a clock case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clock' is slang for the face, so the veil is a cover for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A veil worn by some Muslim women hides the face, which is slang 'clock'.

clue.text: Met challenge of equipment and came first

parts.note: tack is the saddle and bridle equipment of a horse
led means came first, was in front

explanation.surface: A rider took on the equipment and was first home.
explanation.definitionFit: To deal with a problem is to confront it head on.
